audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for mission discourse: twelve apostles, authority, Israel mission, freely received/freely give, hospitality, sheep among wolves, Spirit speech, endurance, fear not, Gehenna, sparrows, confession, sword/division, taking cross, losing/finding life, receiving emissaries.

verses.restored: Calling his twelve disciples, he gave them authority over unclean spirits, to cast them out and to heal every disease and every weakness.

familiar.text: And when he had called unto him his twelve disciples, he gave them power against unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal all manner of sickness and all manner of disease.

modern.text: And calling His twelve disciples to Him, Jesus gave them authority over unclean spirits, so that they could drive them out and heal every disease and sickness.

original.text: Καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος τοὺς δώδεκα μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς ἐξουσίαν πνευμάτων ἀκαθάρτων ὥστε ἐκβάλλειν αὐτὰ καὶ θεραπεύειν πᾶσαν νόσον καὶ πᾶσαν μαλακίαν.

verses.restored: The names of the twelve apostles are these: first Simon, called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James son of Zebedee and John his brother;

familiar.text: Now the names of the twelve apostles are these; The first, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother;

modern.text: These are the names of the twelve apostles: first Simon, called Peter, and his brother Andrew; James son of Zebedee, and his brother John;

original.text: τῶν δὲ δώδεκα ἀποστόλων τὰ ὀνόματά ἐστιν ταῦτα· πρῶτος Σίμων ὁ λεγόμενος Πέτρος καὶ Ἀνδρέας ὁ ἀδελφὸς ⸀αὐτοῦ, Ἰάκωβος ὁ τοῦ Ζεβεδαίου καὶ Ἰωάννης ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ,

verses.restored: Philip and Bartholomew; Thomas and Matthew the tax collector; James son of Alphaeus and Thaddaeus;

familiar.text: Philip, and Bartholomew; Thomas, and Matthew the publican; James the son of Alphaeus, and Lebbaeus, whose surname was Thaddaeus;

modern.text: Philip and Bartholomew; Thomas and Matthew the tax collector; James son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus;

original.text: Φίλιππος καὶ Βαρθολομαῖος, Θωμᾶς καὶ Μαθθαῖος ὁ τελώνης, Ἰάκωβος ὁ τοῦ Ἁλφαίου καὶ ⸀Θαδδαῖος,

verses.restored: Simon the Cananaean/Zealot and Judas Iscariot, who also handed him over.

familiar.text: Simon the Canaanite, and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.

modern.text: Simon the Zealot, and Judas Iscariot, who betrayed Jesus. The Ministry of the Twelve (Mark 6:7–13; Luke 9:1–6)

original.text: Σίμων ὁ ⸀Καναναῖος καὶ Ἰούδας ⸀ὁ Ἰσκαριώτης ὁ καὶ παραδοὺς αὐτόν.

verses.restored: These twelve Jesus sent out, instructing them, saying, Do not go into a way of nations and do not enter a city of Samaritans,

familiar.text: These twelve Jesus sent forth, and commanded them, saying, Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not:

modern.text: These twelve Jesus sent out with the following instructions: “Do not go onto the road of the Gentiles or enter any town of the Samaritans.

original.text: Τούτους τοὺς δώδεκα ἀπέστειλεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς παραγγείλας αὐτοῖς λέγων· Εἰς ὁδὸν ἐθνῶν μὴ ἀπέλθητε καὶ εἰς πόλιν Σαμαριτῶν μὴ εἰσέλθητε·

verses.restored: but go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.

familiar.text: But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.

modern.text: Go rather to the lost sheep of Israel.

original.text: πορεύεσθε δὲ μᾶλλον πρὸς τὰ πρόβατα τὰ ἀπολωλότα οἴκου Ἰσραήλ.

verses.restored: As you go, proclaim, saying, The reign of the heavens has drawn near.

familiar.text: And as ye go, preach, saying, The kingdom of heaven is at hand.

modern.text: As you go, preach this message: ‘The kingdom of heaven is near.’

original.text: πορευόμενοι δὲ κηρύσσετε λέγοντες ὅτι Ἤγγικεν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν.

verses.restored: Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse those with skin disease, cast out unclean spirits. Freely you received; freely give.

familiar.text: Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, cast out devils: freely ye have received, freely give.

modern.text: Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse the lepers, drive out demons. Freely you have received; freely give.

original.text: ἀσθενοῦντας θεραπεύετε, ⸂νεκροὺς ἐγείρετε⸃, λεπροὺς καθαρίζετε, δαιμόνια ἐκβάλλετε· δωρεὰν ἐλάβετε, δωρεὰν δότε.

verses.restored: Do not acquire gold, silver, or copper in your belts,

familiar.text: Provide neither gold, nor silver, nor brass in your purses,

modern.text: Do not carry any gold or silver or copper in your belts.

original.text: μὴ κτήσησθε χρυσὸν μηδὲ ἄργυρον μηδὲ χαλκὸν εἰς τὰς ζώνας ὑμῶν,

verses.restored: no bag for the way, nor two tunics, sandals, or staff; for the worker is worthy of his food.

familiar.text: Nor scrip for your journey, neither two coats, neither shoes, nor yet staves: for the workman is worthy of his meat.

modern.text: Take no bag for the road, or second tunic, or sandals, or staff; for the worker is worthy of his provisions.

original.text: μὴ πήραν εἰς ὁδὸν μηδὲ δύο χιτῶνας μηδὲ ὑποδήματα μηδὲ ⸀ῥάβδον· ἄξιος γὰρ ὁ ἐργάτης τῆς τροφῆς ⸀αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: Whatever city or village you enter, inquire who in it is worthy, and remain there until you leave.

familiar.text: And into whatsoever city or town ye shall enter, enquire who in it is worthy; and there abide till ye go thence.

modern.text: Whatever town or village you enter, find out who is worthy there and stay at his house until you move on.

original.text: εἰς ἣν δʼ ἂν πόλιν ἢ κώμην εἰσέλθητε, ἐξετάσατε τίς ἐν αὐτῇ ἄξιός ἐστιν· κἀκεῖ μείνατε ἕως ἂν ἐξέλθητε.

verses.restored: Entering the house, greet it.

familiar.text: And when ye come into an house, salute it.

modern.text: As you enter the home, greet its occupants.

original.text: εἰσερχόμενοι δὲ εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν ἀσπάσασθε αὐτήν·

verses.restored: If the house is worthy, let your peace come upon it; but if it is not worthy, let your peace return to you.

familiar.text: And if the house be worthy, let your peace come upon it: but if it be not worthy, let your peace return to you.

modern.text: If the home is worthy, let your peace rest on it; but if it is not, let your peace return to you.

original.text: καὶ ἐὰν μὲν ᾖ ἡ οἰκία ἀξία, ἐλθάτω ἡ εἰρήνη ὑμῶν ἐπʼ αὐτήν· ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ᾖ ἀξία, ἡ εἰρήνη ὑμῶν ⸀πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐπιστραφήτω.

verses.restored: Whoever does not receive you or hear your words, as you go out of that house or city, shake off the dust from your feet.

familiar.text: And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words, when ye depart out of that house or city, shake off the dust of your feet.

modern.text: And if anyone will not welcome you or heed your words, shake the dust off your feet when you leave that home or town.

original.text: καὶ ὃς ⸀ἂν μὴ δέξηται ὑμᾶς μηδὲ ἀκούσῃ τοὺς λόγους ὑμῶν, ἐξερχόμενοι ⸀ἔξω τῆς οἰκίας ἢ τῆς πόλεως ἐκείνης ἐκτινάξατε τὸν κονιορτὸν τῶν ποδῶν ὑμῶν.

verses.restored: Amen, I say to you: it will be more bearable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah in the day of judgment than for that city.

familiar.text: Verily I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment, than for that city.

modern.text: Truly I tell you, it will be more bearable for Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgment than for that town. Sheep among Wolves (2 Timothy 1:3–12)

original.text: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀνεκτότερον ἔσται γῇ Σοδόμων καὶ Γομόρρων ἐν ἡμέρᾳ κρίσεως ἢ τῇ πόλει ἐκείνῃ.

verses.restored: Look, I send you out as sheep in the midst of wolves; therefore become wise as serpents and unmixed/innocent as doves.

familiar.text: Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves: be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves.

modern.text: Behold, I am sending you out like sheep among wolves; therefore be as shrewd as snakes and as innocent as doves.

original.text: Ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ἀποστέλλω ὑμᾶς ὡς πρόβατα ἐν μέσῳ λύκων· γίνεσθε οὖν φρόνιμοι ὡς οἱ ὄφεις καὶ ἀκέραιοι ὡς αἱ περιστεραί.

verses.restored: Beware of people, for they will hand you over to councils and flog you in their synagogues.

familiar.text: But beware of men: for they will deliver you up to the councils, and they will scourge you in their synagogues;

modern.text: But beware of men; for they will hand you over to their councils and flog you in their synagogues.

original.text: προσέχετε δὲ ἀπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων· παραδώσουσιν γὰρ ὑμᾶς εἰς συνέδρια, καὶ ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς αὐτῶν μαστιγώσουσιν ὑμᾶς·

verses.restored: You will be brought before governors and kings because of me, as a testimony to them and to the nations.

familiar.text: And ye shall be brought before governors and kings for my sake, for a testimony against them and the Gentiles.

modern.text: On My account, you will be brought before governors and kings as witnesses to them and to the Gentiles.

original.text: καὶ ἐπὶ ἡγεμόνας δὲ καὶ βασιλεῖς ἀχθήσεσθε ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτοῖς καὶ τοῖς ἔθνεσιν.

verses.restored: When they hand you over, do not worry about how or what you should speak, for what you should speak will be given to you in that hour.

familiar.text: But when they deliver you up, take no thought how or what ye shall speak: for it shall be given you in that same hour what ye shall speak.

modern.text: But when they hand you over, do not worry about how to respond or what to say. In that hour you will be given what to say.

original.text: ὅταν δὲ ⸀παραδῶσιν ὑμᾶς, μὴ μεριμνήσητε πῶς ἢ τί λαλήσητε· δοθήσεται γὰρ ὑμῖν ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ τί ⸀λαλήσητε·

verses.restored: For it is not you speaking, but the Spirit of your Father speaking in you.

familiar.text: For it is not ye that speak, but the Spirit of your Father which speaketh in you.

modern.text: For it will not be you speaking, but the Spirit of your Father speaking through you.

original.text: οὐ γὰρ ὑμεῖς ἐστε οἱ λαλοῦντες ἀλλὰ τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ πατρὸς ὑμῶν τὸ λαλοῦν ἐν ὑμῖν.

verses.restored: Brother will hand over brother, and father child; children will rise up against parents and bring about their death.

familiar.text: And the brother shall deliver up the brother to death, and the father the child: and the children shall rise up against their parents, and cause them to be put to death.

modern.text: Brother will betray brother to death, and a father his child; children will rise against their parents and have them put to death.

original.text: παραδώσει δὲ ἀδελφὸς ἀδελφὸν εἰς θάνατον καὶ πατὴρ τέκνον, καὶ ἐπαναστήσονται τέκνα ἐπὶ γονεῖς καὶ θανατώσουσιν αὐτούς.

verses.restored: You will be hated by all because of my name, but the one enduring to the end will be saved.

familiar.text: And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake: but he that endureth to the end shall be saved.

modern.text: You will be hated by everyone because of My name, but the one who perseveres to the end will be saved.

original.text: καὶ ἔσεσθε μισούμενοι ὑπὸ πάντων διὰ τὸ ὄνομά μου· ὁ δὲ ὑπομείνας εἰς τέλος οὗτος σωθήσεται.

verses.restored: When they persecute you in this city, flee to the next; for amen, I say to you, you will not finish the cities of Israel until the Son of Humanity comes.

familiar.text: But when they persecute you in this city, flee ye into another: for verily I say unto you, Ye shall not have gone over the cities of Israel, till the Son of man be come.

modern.text: When they persecute you in one town, flee to the next. Truly I tell you, you will not reach all the towns of Israel before the Son of Man comes.

original.text: ὅταν δὲ διώκωσιν ὑμᾶς ἐν τῇ πόλει ταύτῃ, φεύγετε εἰς τὴν ⸀ἑτέραν· ἀμὴν γὰρ λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐ μὴ τελέσητε τὰς πόλεις ⸀τοῦ Ἰσραὴλ ἕως ⸀ἂν ἔλθῃ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.

verses.restored: A disciple is not above the teacher, nor a servant above the lord.

familiar.text: The disciple is not above his master, nor the servant above his lord.

modern.text: A disciple is not above his teacher, nor a servant above his master.

original.text: Οὐκ ἔστιν μαθητὴς ὑπὲρ τὸν διδάσκαλον οὐδὲ δοῦλος ὑπὲρ τὸν κύριον αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: It is enough for the disciple to become like the teacher, and the servant like the lord. If they called the master of the house Beelzebul, how much more the members of his household.

familiar.text: It is enough for the disciple that he be as his master, and the servant as his lord. If they have called the master of the house Beelzebub, how much more shall they call them of his household?

modern.text: It is enough for a disciple to be like his teacher, and a servant like his master. If the head of the house has been called Beelzebul, how much more the members of his household! Fear God Alone (Luke 12:4–7)

original.text: ἀρκετὸν τῷ μαθητῇ ἵνα γένηται ὡς ὁ διδάσκαλος αὐτοῦ, καὶ ὁ δοῦλος ὡς ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ. εἰ τὸν οἰκοδεσπότην Βεελζεβοὺλ ⸀ἐπεκάλεσαν, πόσῳ μᾶλλον τοὺς οἰκιακοὺς αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: Therefore do not fear them; for nothing is covered that will not be unveiled, and hidden that will not be known.

familiar.text: Fear them not therefore: for there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed; and hid, that shall not be known.

modern.text: So do not be afraid of them. For there is nothing concealed that will not be disclosed, and nothing hidden that will not be made known.

original.text: Μὴ οὖν φοβηθῆτε αὐτούς· οὐδὲν γάρ ἐστιν κεκαλυμμένον ὃ οὐκ ἀποκαλυφθήσεται, καὶ κρυπτὸν ὃ οὐ γνωσθήσεται.

verses.restored: What I tell you in darkness, speak in light; and what you hear in the ear, proclaim on the rooftops.

familiar.text: What I tell you in darkness, that speak ye in light: and what ye hear in the ear, that preach ye upon the housetops.

modern.text: What I tell you in the dark, speak in the daylight; what is whispered in your ear, proclaim from the housetops.

original.text: ὃ λέγω ὑμῖν ἐν τῇ σκοτίᾳ, εἴπατε ἐν τῷ φωτί· καὶ ὃ εἰς τὸ οὖς ἀκούετε, κηρύξατε ἐπὶ τῶν δωμάτων.

verses.restored: Do not fear those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul; rather fear the one able to destroy both soul and body in Gehenna.

familiar.text: And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.

modern.text: Do not be afraid of those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul. Instead, fear the One who can destroy both soul and body in hell.

original.text: καὶ μὴ ⸀φοβεῖσθε ἀπὸ τῶν ἀποκτεννόντων τὸ σῶμα τὴν δὲ ψυχὴν μὴ δυναμένων ἀποκτεῖναι· ⸁φοβεῖσθε δὲ μᾶλλον τὸν δυνάμενον ⸀καὶ ψυχὴν ⸁καὶ σῶμα ἀπολέσαι ἐν γεέννῃ.

verses.restored: Are not two sparrows sold for an assarion? Yet not one of them falls to the earth apart from your Father.

familiar.text: Are not two sparrows sold for a farthing? and one of them shall not fall on the ground without your Father.

modern.text: Are not two sparrows sold for a penny? Yet not one of them will fall to the ground apart from the will of your Father.

original.text: οὐχὶ δύο στρουθία ἀσσαρίου πωλεῖται; καὶ ἓν ἐξ αὐτῶν οὐ πεσεῖται ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ἄνευ τοῦ πατρὸς ὑμῶν.

verses.restored: Even the hairs of your head are all numbered.

familiar.text: But the very hairs of your head are all numbered.

modern.text: And even the very hairs of your head are all numbered.

original.text: ὑμῶν δὲ καὶ αἱ τρίχες τῆς κεφαλῆς πᾶσαι ἠριθμημέναι εἰσίν.

verses.restored: Therefore do not fear; you are worth more than many sparrows.

familiar.text: Fear ye not therefore, ye are of more value than many sparrows.

modern.text: So do not be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows. Confessing Christ (Luke 12:8–12)

original.text: μὴ οὖν ⸀φοβεῖσθε· πολλῶν στρουθίων διαφέρετε ὑμεῖς.

verses.restored: Everyone who confesses me before people, I also will confess before my Father in the heavens.

familiar.text: Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven.

modern.text: Therefore everyone who confesses Me before men, I will also confess him before My Father in heaven.

original.text: Πᾶς οὖν ὅστις ὁμολογήσει ἐν ἐμοὶ ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ὁμολογήσω κἀγὼ ἐν αὐτῷ ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ πατρός μου τοῦ ⸀ἐν οὐρανοῖς·

verses.restored: Whoever denies me before people, I also will deny before my Father in the heavens.

familiar.text: But whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father which is in heaven.

modern.text: But whoever denies Me before men, I will also deny him before My Father in heaven. Not Peace but a Sword (Micah 7:1–6; Luke 12:49–53)

original.text: ὅστις ⸂δʼ ἂν⸃ ἀρνήσηταί με ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ἀρνήσομαι ⸂κἀγὼ αὐτὸν⸃ ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ πατρός μου τοῦ ⸀ἐν οὐρανοῖς.

verses.restored: Do not think that I came to bring peace on the earth; I did not come to bring peace but a sword.

familiar.text: Think not that I am come to send peace on earth: I came not to send peace, but a sword.

modern.text: Do not assume that I have come to bring peace to the earth; I have not come to bring peace, but a sword.

original.text: Μὴ νομίσητε ὅτι ἦλθον βαλεῖν εἰρήνην ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν· οὐκ ἦλθον βαλεῖν εἰρήνην ἀλλὰ μάχαιραν.

verses.restored: For I came to divide a man against his father, a daughter against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.

familiar.text: For I am come to set a man at variance against his father, and the daughter against her mother, and the daughter in law against her mother in law.

modern.text: For I have come to turn ‘a man against his father, a daughter against her mother, a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.

original.text: ἦλθον γὰρ διχάσαι ἄνθρωπον κατὰ τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ καὶ θυγατέρα κατὰ τῆς μητρὸς αὐτῆς καὶ νύμφην κατὰ τῆς πενθερᾶς αὐτῆς,

verses.restored: A person's enemies will be members of his own household.

familiar.text: And a man’s foes shall be they of his own household.

modern.text: A man’s enemies will be the members of his own household.’

original.text: καὶ ἐχθροὶ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου οἱ οἰκιακοὶ αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: The one loving father or mother more than me is not worthy of me, and the one loving son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me.

familiar.text: He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me: and he that loveth son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me.

modern.text: Anyone who loves his father or mother more than Me is not worthy of Me; anyone who loves his son or daughter more than Me is not worthy of Me;

original.text: ὁ φιλῶν πατέρα ἢ μητέρα ὑπὲρ ἐμὲ οὐκ ἔστιν μου ἄξιος· καὶ ὁ φιλῶν υἱὸν ἢ θυγατέρα ὑπὲρ ἐμὲ οὐκ ἔστιν μου ἄξιος·

verses.restored: Whoever does not take his cross and follow after me is not worthy of me.

familiar.text: And he that taketh not his cross, and followeth after me, is not worthy of me.

modern.text: and anyone who does not take up his cross and follow Me is not worthy of Me.

original.text: καὶ ὃς οὐ λαμβάνει τὸν σταυρὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀκολουθεῖ ὀπίσω μου, οὐκ ἔστιν μου ἄξιος.

verses.restored: The one finding his life/soul will lose it, and the one losing his life/soul because of me will find it.

familiar.text: He that findeth his life shall lose it: and he that loseth his life for my sake shall find it.

modern.text: Whoever finds his life will lose it, and whoever loses his life for My sake will find it. The Reward of Service (2 Kings 4:8–17)

original.text: ὁ εὑρὼν τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἀπολέσει αὐτήν, καὶ ὁ ἀπολέσας τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ εὑρήσει αὐτήν.

verses.restored: The one receiving you receives me, and the one receiving me receives the One who sent me.

familiar.text: He that receiveth you receiveth me, and he that receiveth me receiveth him that sent me.

modern.text: He who receives you receives Me, and he who receives Me receives the One who sent Me.

original.text: Ὁ δεχόμενος ὑμᾶς ἐμὲ δέχεται, καὶ ὁ ἐμὲ δεχόμενος δέχεται τὸν ἀποστείλαντά με.

verses.restored: The one receiving a prophet in the name of a prophet will receive a prophet's reward, and the one receiving a righteous person in the name of a righteous person will receive a righteous person's reward.

familiar.text: He that receiveth a prophet in the name of a prophet shall receive a prophet’s reward; and he that receiveth a righteous man in the name of a righteous man shall receive a righteous man’s reward.

modern.text: Whoever receives a prophet because he is a prophet will receive a prophet’s reward, and whoever receives a righteous man because he is a righteous man will receive a righteous man’s reward.

original.text: ὁ δεχόμενος προφήτην εἰς ὄνομα προφήτου μισθὸν προφήτου λήμψεται, καὶ ὁ δεχόμενος δίκαιον εἰς ὄνομα δικαίου μισθὸν δικαίου λήμψεται.

verses.restored: Whoever gives one of these little ones only a cup of cold water in the name of a disciple, amen, I say to you, he will certainly not lose his reward.

familiar.text: And whosoever shall give to drink unto one of these little ones a cup of cold water only in the name of a disciple, verily I say unto you, he shall in no wise lose his reward.

modern.text: And if anyone gives even a cup of cold water to one of these little ones because he is My disciple, truly I tell you, he will never lose his reward.”

original.text: καὶ ὃς ⸀ἂν ποτίσῃ ἕνα τῶν μικρῶν τούτων ποτήριον ψυχροῦ μόνον εἰς ὄνομα μαθητοῦ, ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐ μὴ ἀπολέσῃ τὸν μισθὸν αὐτοῦ.
